_note: S5.4 draws THREE gates because the next move differs — send one, wait for
one, or go read the comments that came back. The code already split the
server's four PRECONDITION_FAILED messages into four `blockedReason`s, and
then rendered three of them as one shape: a warning TOAST that described the
way out in prose ("Open the Review panel (press R)") and dismissed the
reason in the same effect. All three boards draw a modal with the door in it.
WHAT MOVED: `PublishGateModal` (src/editor/shell/modals/PublishGateModal.tsx)
is new, and `APPROVAL_GATE_TOASTS` in useExportHandlers is gone with the
effect that raised it. That effect called `dismissBlock()` immediately, so no
dialog could ever have been driven off `blockedReason` while it stood. The
modal is mounted by StudioPanels, which already receives `publishJob` for the
Publish panel and already owns the `ui:switch-tab` event every gate's primary
fires. `stale-approval` is untouched — it is the one gate with something to
over-ride, and it keeps StaleApprovalModal.
Probe, not the live app: the gate only opens when the DASHBOARD refuses a
publish, which needs a site, a round in the wrong state, and a real
`sites.publish` rejection. The probe mounts the real modal with the reason
the server would have sent.
NOT anchored, and why:
307:2194 the card frame — its `rounded-[16px]` belongs to the DIALOG, and
the dialog frame is MODAL_FRAME_BASE_CLASS, shared by every modal in the
product at radius 12 (the same call publish-confirm's recipe records for
914:4507). The code therefore splits it: the shared frame carries the
radius and the 520 width, an inner block carries the board's 32 gutter,
30 top and 14 stack. The gutter is still measured — 307:2196 is 456 wide,
which IS 520 less two 32s.
390:3837 the scrim — exported as an opaque `--flowbite/gray/900` because
Figma bakes layer opacity out. A 100% black scrim is export noise.
307:2193 the board root — the 1440 page behind the dialog.
COPY: the board's sentence, with the round's real client in place of
"Sara (sara@client.com)" and a fallback for a round that cannot be read.
"once she approves" is written "once they approve" — the product does not
know a reviewer's gender.
COPY DEVIATION, deliberate — `check-board-copy` flags it, and it is the
sample-data rule rather than drift: the boards write "once SHE approves"
and "resolve HER comments" because the board's reviewer is called Sara.
Nothing in the product knows a reviewer's gender — `reviewerName` is a
string — so the shipped sentence is "once they approve" / "resolve their
comments". The SHAPE is conformed; the pronoun is bound to the persona.
